Description: Support machine-based data deposit and metadata transfer via REST API
Remarks: NRP API broken in current release. Local patch tested and working; upstream integration uncertain.
Note: Enables automated, scalable submission directly from instruments and laboratory systems
Reference: NRP API docs; local patch (location TBD)

Description: Assign DOI to published Activity records via DataCite integration
Remarks: Wired but untested — requires DataCite sandbox account
Note: Supports reliable citation and long-term referencing

Description: Support ePIC handles or similar persistent identifiers for hierarchical sub-parts of datasets where granular referencing is needed
Remarks: Discussed but not implemented
Note: Supports granular citation of dataset sub-components

Description: Support open, embargoed, restricted, and metadata-only access levels with configurable per-record visibility
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM access model supports open / embargoed / restricted out of the box
Note: Enables sharing of both open and sensitive data; metadata remains publicly visible regardless of file access

Description: Federated authentication and role-based authorization with institutional identity and affiliation verification
Remarks: Built-in — NRP integrates with e-INFRA CZ AAI (eduGAIN / ORCID); community-level role-based access control available via InvenioRDM
Note: Ensures secure and controlled access to restricted data

Description: Platform-level support for serializing and exporting records in standard interchange formats
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM/NRP provides DataCite XML, Dublin Core, and JSON-LD export endpoints out of the box
Note: Enables inclusion in external discovery services and aggregators

Description: Platform-level full-text search and field-based filtering across all published records
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM/NRP provides OpenSearch-backed full-text search and field filtering out of the box
Note: Enables efficient discovery of relevant datasets

Requirement: Record detail page and file preview
Description: Display record metadata and basic file preview on the record landing page before download or access request
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM provides record landing pages with metadata display and file previewer for common formats
Note: Allows users to assess dataset relevance before download or access request
Derived from specification: Row 10: Dataset preview and metadata display

Description: Platform-level export of record metadata in standard machine-readable formats via content negotiation
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM supports JSON, DataCite XML, and Dublin Core export via content negotiation on record endpoints
Note: Supports automated processing and reuse of metadata by external systems and aggregators

Description: Maintain metadata visibility and persistent identifier resolution after record withdrawal or deletion
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM displays a tombstone page with removal reason when a record is withdrawn; DOI continues to resolve
Note: Preserves citation integrity and transparency

Description: Provide statistics on dataset access, downloads, and views per record
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM tracks view and download counts per record via invenio-stats
Note: Helps assess dataset impact and usage patterns

Description: Platform-level support for complex queries — boolean operators, range filters, and nested field queries — via OpenSearch
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM/NRP exposes OpenSearch query DSL; complex queries supported via API
Note: Improves discovery for complex queries beyond basic field filtering
Reference: InvenioRDM search docs; OpenSearch query DSL

Description: Support multiple versions of a record with distinct persistent identifiers and a navigable version history
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM supports record versioning; each version receives a distinct DOI; version history is displayed on the record landing page
Note: Allows updates while preserving previous versions for citation

Description: Store and serve files of any format without format-specific constraints
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM stores files as binary objects with no format restrictions; file type identified by MIME type and filename extension. File deduplication is not supported — invenio-files-rest does not implement content-addressable storage, so identical files uploaded separately are stored as distinct physical copies.
Note: Reflects the variety of data formats produced in materials science workflows
Derived from specification: Row 20: Support for heterogeneous data types

Description: Enable storage and access for datasets at GB–TB scale
Remarks: Supported via S3-compatible object storage backend; multipart upload supported; practical size limits depend on NRP instance configuration and storage quota
Note: Required for instrument and simulation data typical in materials science
Reference: NRP storage configuration docs; invenio-s3 package

Description: Support organization of records into communities with distinct governance policies, curation roles, and access rules
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM communities provide owner/curator/reader roles, submission review workflows, and community-scoped search
Note: Enables domain-specific governance, curation, and access control

Description: Allow multiple users to contribute to and edit Activity records with defined roles and shared ownership
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM supports shared record ownership and community curator roles; multiple users can be granted edit access to a record
Note: Supports team-based research workflows and shared responsibility for dataset curation

Description: Platform-level draft/publish workflow with state transitions and pre-publish validation hooks
Remarks: Built-in — InvenioRDM draft/publish state machine supports pre-publish validators; curator review step available via community submission workflow
Note: Ensures controlled, validated publication of Activity records
Reference: InvenioRDM draft/publish docs; InvenioRDM communities submission workflow
Derived from specification: Row 28: Structured submission workflow (auto-check + curator review)

Description: Platform support for establishing typed persistent identifier relationships between records
Remarks: Provided via oarepo pid-relation package; currently functional. Known limitation: pid-relations require the target record to be in registered (published) state — linking to draft records is not supported; this is an upstream oarepo issue deferred to summer 2027. Linked records must be stored in the same repository — cross-repository PID linking is not supported. Export to CCMM is not automatically supported; explicit mapping to related_resource or provenance fields is required depending on use case (CESNET NRP-CZ Discussion #15).
Note: Enables inter-record provenance chains and hierarchical structures between Activity records; required for parent_activities linking to function

Description: Platform support for hierarchical publishing of related records with parent/child publishing semantics propagating through the hierarchy
Remarks: NRP hierarchical records support is planned for approximately November 2026; not yet available. Distinct from PID linking (PLTREQ-019) — hierarchical records govern publishing lifecycle propagation, not just identifier resolution. Confirmed "not yet implemented in CESNET Invenio repositories" by CESNET authors (CESNET NRP-CZ Discussion #15, Miroslav Šimek, CESNET). Export to CCMM is not automatically supported — mapping may split across related_resource and provenance fields depending on use case.
Note: Enables structured hierarchical data publication where parent record state governs child record visibility

Description: NRP InvenioRDM and all dependencies can be installed and built from official upstream release packages without local patches
Remarks: Current state: at least one component (API ingestion endpoint) requires a local patch to function. Community packaging process and release schedule are not publicly documented and are opaque to DANTEc developers. This is an implicit infrastructure dependency of all platform requirements.
Note: Prerequisite for reliable and maintainable deployment; local patches introduce maintenance burden and are not sustainable

Description: Platform support for creating a new draft record from an existing published record, preserving metadata for adaptation and reuse
Remarks: Whether this is available as a built-in NRP feature or requires custom implementation is not yet confirmed; requires investigation before closure.
Note: Enables data reuse workflows where researchers adapt existing datasets for new experiments without re-entering metadata

Description: Platform support for linking records to external or internal resources via the CCMM related_resource field, with typed relation types from the vocabs.ccmm.cz registry
Remarks: Built-in — CESNET Invenio implements related_resource as the standard mechanism for linking records to external or internal resources. Supports typed relation types (IsDerivedFrom, IsPartOf, HasPart, etc.) from the vocabs.ccmm.cz registry; maps automatically to CCMM 1.1.0 export. Known limitation: all related resources are stored in a single flat list with no mechanism to group links by context or type. A vocabulary of controlled external repository targets is not natively supported — any URL is valid, so identifier decomposition for machine-to-machine federation (e.g. OPTIMADE, MC4EU) requires additional per-platform integration work (see DANREQ-005). (CESNET NRP-CZ Discussion #15, Miroslav Šimek, CESNET)
Note: Provides the linking layer for publication/software references (DANREQ-010) and discovery-level external platform interoperability (DANREQ-005); the latter requires additional exchange protocol work beyond linking
Reference: CESNET NRP-CZ Discussion #15; CCMM related_resource field specification; vocabs.ccmm.cz registry
Derived from specification: Row 14: Interoperability with domain platforms; Row 22: Linking datasets to publications and software

Description: Platform-level support for vocabulary terms with parent/child relationships, enabling nested term hierarchies via parent_id or equivalent fields in the NRP vocabulary service
Remarks: Not yet verified through testing. InvenioRDM vocabulary service nominally supports hierarchy.parent_id and hierarchy.level fields, but whether this is reliably functional in the NRP/oarepo environment is unknown. This is a design-informing requirement — if hierarchy is supported, DANTEc controlled vocabularies can use nested structures for faceted navigation; if not, flat vocabulary design is required.
Note: Required to inform vocabulary term depth and facet hierarchy design decisions in DANTEc
